response.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    c.customer_id,
    c.gender,
    COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM Customers c
  INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender
),
gender_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    gender,
    SUM(order_count) as gender_order_total
  FROM customer_orders
  GROUP BY gender
),
shares AS (
  SELECT 
    co.customer_id,
    co.gender,
    co.order_count,
    CAST(co.order_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / CAST(gt.gender_order_total AS DECIMAL(19,4)) as share
  FROM customer_orders co
  JOIN gender_totals gt ON co.gender = gt.gender
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as average_share
  FROM shares
)
SELECT 
  s.customer_id,
  s.gender,
  s.order_count,
  s.share,
  s.share - a.average_share as gap_above_average
FROM shares s
CROSS JOIN avg_share a
WHERE s.share > a.average_share
ORDER BY gap_above_average DESC
LIMIT 10;

alternatives.interpretation: The 'average share' could be calculated within each gender group instead of globally, so customers are compared only against the average share of other customers in their same gender.
